about.title: Santa Ana Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Santa Ana comes without warning, the paperwork tends to arrive before the grief has any room to settle. Public records show 33 traffic deaths in the city during 2025. Corridors such as 1st Street, Bristol Street, and both directions of I-5 carry the heaviest collision counts, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. account for the largest share of reported crashes. Behind each of those figures is a household now short one income, one driver, one voice at the dinner table. California law gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim; certain dependents and heirs may follow. That claim is civil and moves on its own track, separate from any criminal case a prosecutor might pursue. Two years from the date of death is the general deadline, and the window shrinks considerably when a city, county, or other public agency is involved. Our team works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Ana Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death action, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out standing early, before anyone files the wrong paperwork.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but the timeline is much shorter when a government entity such as a city or county is a party. We help protect those dates from the start.

items.title: Full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial costs, California recognizes lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Our team can document each category rather than settling for the obvious expenses alone.

items.question: The crash happened on I-5 in Santa Ana and the other driver was arrested. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, if your family wants to recover losses. A criminal case is brought by the prosecutor and can result in penalties for the driver, but it does not pay your funeral costs or replace lost support. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action your family controls, and it can proceed regardless of how the criminal matter turns out.

items.question: My sibling died in Santa Ana. Can I be the one to file?
items.answer: It depends on who else survives them. California gives first priority to a spouse or domestic partner and children; if none exist, certain dependents and heirs may have standing. We can review your family situation and tell you where you fall in that order.

items.question: How long do we have to act in Orange County?
items.answer: The general rule is two years from the date of death. If a public agency was involved, such as a city vehicle or a road maintained by the county or state, a government claim must typically be filed within a much shorter period first. Because of that, it is wise to speak with us well before the two-year mark.
